rv.q: This theatre describes the play as a “macabre comedy” and that is what is rendered on stage. The blind, seated Hamm (Douglas Hodge, returning to the stage after more than a decade) is not so much a tyrant as an aged thespian, even if he whistles for his limping servant, Clov (Mathew Horne), and consigns his parents to dustbins.

For the duration of the play’s ninety minutes, the set works almost like an optical illusion, and it is truly terrific that Bausor has managed to instil a gloomy scene with such character. The costumes do similarly great work in depicting the decrepit premise, yet it is the makeup design which provides the strongest characterisation.
